name: Grasim Industries Ltd.
business_summary: Aditya Birla Group flagship holding company with a majority stake in UltraTech (cement) and Aditya Birla Capital (financial services), plus standalone businesses: viscose staple fibre (VSF) and fashion yarn, chemicals (caustic soda, chlorine derivatives, epichlorohydrin), Birla Opus decorative paints (loss-making build-out), B2B e-commerce (Birla Pivot), renewables and textiles. Q1 FY27 consolidated sales Rs48,716 cr, EBITDA Rs11,152 cr, PAT Rs3,846 cr; Q2 results not yet reported. Mcap Rs2.18 lakh cr, P/E 38; promoters raised stake to 45.07% (28 Sep).

exposures.mechanism: Consolidated interest Rs4,298 cr/quarter (Jun 2026) incl. NBFC and UltraTech; standalone leverage rising with paint, chemical and renewable capex. +25bp on ~Rs60-70k cr floating non-financial debt (model estimate) -> -Rs150-175 cr = -1.5% PBT; plus holdco/long-duration P/E 38 -> -1.5% -> blended -1.8 incl. ABCAPITAL credit-cycle drag. RBI hiked to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026.

evidence.note: RBI hiked repo 25bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, stance 'calibrated tightening' (Reuters/The Hindu/Moneycontrol headlines)

exposures.mechanism: Paints (Birla Opus), B2B e-commerce, VSF/fashion linkage and ABCAPITAL retail credit; paints ~6-8% of revenue (model estimate) but loss-making so volume ramp raises operating leverage. +5pp urban demand -> paints/B2B revenue +3% and ABCAP loan growth -> consolidated EBITDA +2% -> x1.6 EV/MCap x0.5 -> +1.6.

Direct (non-cement) channel only: decorative paints and building chemicals track housing completions. Cement housing exposure is carried via the ULTRACEMCO holding link, not here. +10% sales -> paints volume +2% -> EBITDA +0.6% of group -> +1.0.

Standalone chemicals (caustic soda is ~2,500 kWh/t, power ~45% of cost) and VSF use captive coal power; seaborne coal +15% -> chemical/VSF cost +4%. Empirical -1.18 (t -1.1) agrees. Cement fuel exposure is via the UltraTech link.
VSF competes with cotton as a fibre; +10% cotton lifts VSF realisations and volumes. VSF ~8% of consolidated revenue (model estimate), EBITDA small; empirical +0.54 (t +0.9).

Chinese export push (+15% volumes/price cuts) pressures caustic soda, chlorine derivatives, epichlorohydrin (ECH commercial production began 21 Oct 2026, import-substituting) and VSF. Chemicals ~12% of EBITDA ex-cement; +15% -> chemicals EBITDA -10% -> -1.2% group -> x1.6 x0.5... -0.8.

evidence.note: Suzlon-Grasim recyclable-blade tie-up, both shares +5% (CNBC TV18/Business Today 4 Nov); ECH commercial production started in Gujarat (HDFC Sky 21 Oct); Birla family raised stake to 45.07% (scanx 28 Sep)

exposures.mechanism: Imported wood pulp for VSF (~35% of VSF cost), imported ECH feed/other chemicals; USD debt in renewables partly hedged. +3% -> VSF/chem cost +1% -> -0.7 incl. UltraTech fuel import (via link).

Paints raw materials (TiO2, monomers, solvents ~30% of paint costs) and caustic-derivative chemicals are crude-linked; paints are currently loss-making so cost inflation deepens losses. Cement diesel/fuel is via the link.
New anti-dumping/safeguard duties on VSF, caustic soda, chlorine derivatives and ECH protect domestic pricing; +1 SSU ~ +3% chemicals EBITDA.

company_links.mechanism: Grasim holds ~56% of UltraTech (model knowledge) worth ~Rs2.0 lakh cr vs Grasim mcap Rs2.18 lakh cr, i.e. ~93% of Grasim's market cap before holding-company discount (20-35%) -> look-through weight ~0.6 (0.45-0.75).
Grasim holds ~52% of Aditya Birla Capital (model knowledge) worth ~Rs0.57 lakh cr (mcap Rs1.09 lakh cr per pack) = ~26% of Grasim mcap; after 30% discount ~0.2.

supply_chain.note: allotted 23.15 cr equity shares to Grasim (24 Sep)

supply_chain.counterparty: Asian Paints, Berger, Kansai, JSW Paints
Wood-pulp suppliers (Canada, Brazil, Indonesia), Chinese VSF/caustic exporters
